checks.label: The page actually loads
checks.question: Will someone who clicks the ad reach the page at all?
checks.method: The navigation response is an HTTP 2xx, and the URL the browser ended on has the same hostname as the one requested (ignoring a leading "www.").
checks.detail: Responded HTTP 200 and stayed on neemans.com.

checks.label: Your tags are installed and firing
checks.question: Are Google Analytics and the Meta Pixel actually on this page?
checks.method: Google Analytics 4 and Meta Pixel must each have sent at least one network request during the session.
checks.detail: Both required tags fired. Google Analytics 4: 13 requests; Meta Pixel: 8 requests.

checks.label: Nothing fires twice
checks.question: Is the page counting the same thing more than once?
checks.method: A SHA-1 fingerprint of vendor + event name + payload, with every param that changes on every hit removed first. Two requests sharing a fingerprint are the same beacon sent twice, not two legitimate events.

checks.label: The data actually arrives
checks.question: Does the data reach the platforms, or does it die on the way?
checks.method: Any tracking request answered with a 4xx or 5xx, plus any request that failed at the transport layer and never got a response at all. Grouped by vendor and status.

checks.label: One account per platform
checks.question: Is the data all landing in the same account, or split across several?
checks.method: For each vendor, count the distinct account / property / pixel IDs seen. More than one means the traffic is being split.

checks.label: Add to cart gets tracked
checks.question: When someone adds to cart, do the ad platforms find out?
checks.method: During the add-to-cart phase specifically, each installed ad platform must have received at least one event matching a commercial-intent pattern. If no add-to-cart button could be found, this is recorded as not applicable rather than pass or fail.
checks.detail: Meta Pixel, Snap Pixel, Criteo received no conversion event after the click.

checks.label: Event names make sense to the platforms
checks.question: Will the ad platforms understand the events they are being sent?
checks.method: Each Meta and GA4 event name is checked for membership in that platform's published standard event vocabulary. Names outside it are custom and cannot drive built-in optimisation.

checks.label: Nothing dead is still running
checks.question: Is the page still sending data to a system that was switched off?
checks.method: Any hit to the Universal Analytics /collect endpoint. Universal Analytics stopped processing data in July 2024; these requests go nowhere.
checks.detail: No traffic to deprecated Universal Analytics endpoints.

aiIssues.title: Google Ads counts non-existent sales as soon as the page opens
aiIssues.detail: Automated ad bidding algorithms will see high conversion numbers that never happened, driving spend toward useless traffic that just opens the link.
aiIssues.businessRisk: Automated ad bidding algorithms will see high conversion numbers that never happened, driving spend toward useless traffic that just opens the link.
aiIssues.technicalEvidence: Google Ads received 8 separate conversion events between 11.7 seconds and 17.4 seconds during initial page load, long before any user click occurred.
aiIssues.recommendedFix: Remove conversion tags assigned to page-load triggers and restrict conversion firing strictly to confirmed purchases.
aiIssues.affectedMetric: Google Ads reported ROAS and cost per acquisition

aiIssues.title: Meta, Snap, and Criteo are completely blind to shopper intent
aiIssues.detail: You cannot retarget high-intent shoppers on Meta, Snap, or Criteo because these platforms never know when a user adds a product to their cart.
aiIssues.businessRisk: You cannot retarget high-intent shoppers on Meta, Snap, or Criteo because these platforms never know when a user adds a product to their cart.
aiIssues.technicalEvidence: When the add to cart button was clicked at 56.3 seconds, zero events were sent to Meta Pixel, Snap Pixel, or Criteo.
aiIssues.recommendedFix: Add standard add_to_cart triggers in Tag Manager for Meta, Snap, and Criteo.
aiIssues.affectedMetric: Meta, Snap, and Criteo retargeting ROAS

aiIssues.title: A single cart add triggers multiple conversion claims in Google Ads
aiIssues.detail: Your reporting will vastly overstate product demand and cart actions, making campaign reporting unreliable.
aiIssues.businessRisk: Your reporting will vastly overstate product demand and cart actions, making campaign reporting unreliable.
aiIssues.technicalEvidence: A single add-to-cart action at 56.3 seconds generated 6 separate conversion calls to Google Ads across multiple account IDs.
aiIssues.recommendedFix: Deduplicate Google Ads triggers so one button click sends exactly one event.

aiIssues.title: Data is split across duplicate Google and Snap account IDs
aiIssues.detail: Your analytics reporting is fractured across two separate Google Analytics accounts and two Snap account IDs, leading to inaccurate performance summaries.
aiIssues.businessRisk: Your analytics reporting is fractured across two separate Google Analytics accounts and two Snap account IDs, leading to inaccurate performance summaries.
aiIssues.technicalEvidence: GA4 tracking sends events to both G-3042L5GP9T and G-VDE0ZFZ4LP, while Snap sends to two distinct account IDs.
aiIssues.recommendedFix: Audit Google Tag Manager and remove secondary or legacy tracking IDs.
aiIssues.affectedMetric: GA4 total session and event counts

headline: Do not put ad spend behind this page yet.
executiveSummary: Your advertising tracking is severely broken and will waste your budget. Google Ads is recording multiple fake sales before a customer even clicks anything on the page. Meanwhile, major ad channels like Meta, Snap, and Criteo receive no data when someone adds a product to their cart.

recommendedNextSteps: Pause paid ad spend directed to this page until tag triggers are fixed.

Configure Meta, Snap, and Criteo pixels to capture add-to-cart events.
Deduplicate Google Ads tags to fire only once per user click.
Remove duplicate GA4 and Snap account IDs from Tag Manager.
